- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next period; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1st–3rd day) when sentiment is volatile; add 1–2% buffer to early predictions.
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to 0.00), model often fails to adjust; force a 1–3 day lagged correction to match sentiment shift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices when sentiment is clustered positive; apply a 2–5% downward adjustment if sentiment average >0.67 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00 over 3+ days, model tends to drift downward; apply upward bias to counteract mean reversion bias.
